faqItems.question: What kinds of activities are there?
faqItems.answer: The source website introduces Tokyo Orienteering, SOP and the Christmas Party, alongside BBQs, cruises and overnight trips. The activities page includes photographs with source links.

faqItems.question: Are there exchanges with Japanese-language schools?
faqItems.answer: The former site describes visitor sessions and joint events with language schools. Public records from 2025 also document exchanges with JET Japanese Language School.

faqItems.question: How can I join a future event?
faqItems.answer: Check the contact information on SNIE’s source website for the latest guidance. Historical event records on this site are not current registration notices.

signature.title: Tokyo Orienteering
signature.description: A major spring outing through Tokyo. Small groups complete missions while visiting sightseeing spots, with plenty of time to talk and get to know one another.

signature.title: SOP — SNIE Olympics
signature.description: SNIE’s sports day features original games devised by students. Four teams compete for the title, and some participants come in costume, making it fun to play and watch.

signature.title: Christmas Party
signature.description: A Christmas party with dresses and suits, games, a buffet and festive decorations. The former website also describes a bingo competition with prizes.

other.title: Summer camp
other.description: An overnight trip to a cooler summer destination. Activities such as catching rainbow trout and cooking curry together help students become closer.

other.title: Snowboard camp
other.description: An overnight trip to a ski resort. The former website describes a beginner-friendly experience, with experienced students helping newcomers learn.

other.title: Autumn BBQ
other.description: An autumn barbecue shared outdoors. It is introduced as an easy opportunity to join in, including for students who could not attend many first-semester events.

other.title: Tokyo Bay cruise
other.description: A summer cruise on Tokyo Bay, with students wearing yukata. The former website also mentions fireworks and making memories together on the water.

other.title: Overnight retreat
other.description: An overnight trip that also thanks the third-year students who helped run SNIE, with gym activities and sightseeing together.

events.note: Descriptions are based on the former public website; these are not upcoming dates or open registrations.

leadership.title: A president’s perspective
leadership.note: Four questions from the former website’s chair interview. The person’s name and term were not stated.

items.question: A few words about the chair?
items.answer: The interview describes an enthusiasm for relationship advice, basketball and eating big meals.

items.question: When did you start taking part?
items.answer: In September of the first year at university, as a member of the SOP event staff.

items.question: Which event is your favorite?
items.answer: Summer camp, for the chance to get to know everyone and enjoy student life together.

items.question: What makes SNIE special?
items.answer: It is easy to settle in after joining midway. The interview says many of the third-year participants at that time had joined in their second year.

languageSchools.title: Connecting with language schools
languageSchools.intro: Playing together at an event or visiting a classroom: the former site describes several ways university students met students learning Japanese.

items.title: Visitor sessions
items.description: Conversation-based exchanges, including visits to Eastwest Japanese Language School.

items.title: Joint events
items.description: Joint outings and year-end gatherings with JET Japanese Language School, as well as participation in SNIE events.

history.intro: Follow SNIE’s exchanges through its former websites and newsletters. Roles, organizations and participation methods on this page belong to the period in which each source was published.
history.heading: Read the former websites
history.body: This collection preserves 22 pages and two PDFs. Text remains in its original language, and the date a page was saved is distinct from an event date. The collection does not contain every historical revision.

presentation.aboutBody: Interested in international exchange? Looking for a community beyond your university, or more ways to enjoy student life? SNIE brings together four clubs from four universities around those shared interests.
presentation.welcomeTitle: Find your own way to join in.
presentation.welcomeBody: Come to make friends or deepen your understanding of other countries. The former website describes SNIE as a relaxed, club-like community where students can enjoy taking part in their own way.
presentation.sourceNote: These introductions draw on the former SNIE website. Photographs and interviews are historical records, not statements of current leadership or upcoming events.
